r25q_34c61d43d1c6a0f0c7.explanation: CASE-BB1FE84A50 (OBS-41317161, 18:33, over 3): two signed review entries conflict on the bowler's-end No-ball call; per protocol note 1929E99B the higher revision (rev 9, No-ball) is active, so initial_call_set is NO_BALL_ONLY. The ball touched the striker's bat (incident log), one run was completed, and the striker's-end Wide call is revoked by Law 22.3.1 (digest C62E6AB0) since bat contact preceded any fielder contact. Effective status NO_BALL; under Law 21.17 (digest 48F22FA6) no dismissal is available, one No-ball extra is scored, the delivery does not count in the over (Law 21.16, digest 796B126C), and the extra is debited to the bowler (digest 8AD4729A). Counterfactual: with no No-ball call, the Wide stands (no bat-contact revocation trigger changes, contact remains BAT), making the delivery a WIDE; the completed run plus the one-run Wide penalty are Wide extras (Laws 22.6-22.7, digest 4F14DF9C), the delivery does not count in the over (Law 22.8, digest F9595A7B), no dismissal is possible, and both runs are debited to the bowler (digest 8AD4729A).

r25q_3d0a7bcd3ac8a03ace.explanation: CASE-9B7A80E095: no No-ball call at the bowler's end, ball touched the striker's bat then broke the wicket, valid fielding appeal was made, dismissal category submitted was Bowled. Under Law 32.1 (digest 83442B4C) a non-No-ball delivery that breaks the wicket after first touching the striker's bat is Bowled; the delivery is legal, counts in the over, and no runs are recorded. Counterfactual: changing no_ball_called to a No-ball call makes the delivery a NO_BALL (Law 21.12 override precedence irrelevant as no Wide was called); under Law 21.17 (digest 48F22FA6) Bowled is unavailable after a No-ball, so dismissal becomes NONE, one No-ball extra is scored (Law 21.14-21.15, digest 6D37A3DE), the ball does not count in the over, and the No-ball extra is debited to the bowler (digest 8AD4729A).

r25q_7685b11e2ad222c6db.explanation: CASE-408357B9C9 (OBS-57183E84, 14:00, over 36): two signed review entries conflict on bat contact; per protocol note 1929E99B the higher revision (18:29, no contact) is active, so observed_contact is NONE. No No-ball or Wide call exists, so the delivery is legal and counts in the over. Two runs were completed, then a fielder's throw at the wicket went for a boundary with agreed allowance 4; the batters had crossed at the instant of the throw, so Law 19.8 (digest A7F3AEEE) subsumes all movement into a 4-run boundary credited to the batter (Law 19.6-19.7, digest A5859EFC). No appeal or wicket event is recorded, so dismissal is NONE. Counterfactual: restoring bat contact does not change the legal status, the boundary allowance of 4 still subsumes the 2 completed runs, and the 4 batter runs, live ball state, and NONE dismissal are unchanged.

r25q_930d634829802e3016.explanation: CASE-3A1E819B2D (OBS-57183E84, 14:00, over 36): the bowler's-end No-ball call (incident log) makes the delivery a NO_BALL; under Law 21.17 (digest 48F22FA6) no dismissal is available, so the run-out attempt off this delivery cannot dismiss. The ball touched the striker's bat, two runs were completed, and a fielder's throw at the wicket went for a boundary with agreed allowance 4; since the batters had crossed at the instant of the throw, Law 19.8 (digest A7F3AEEE) awards allowance 4 plus the run in progress, totalling 5 batter runs (Law 19.6-19.7, digest A5859EFC). One No-ball extra is added (Laws 21.14-21.15, digest 6D37A3DE), the delivery does not count in the over (Law 21.16, digest 796B126C), and the bowler is debited the 4 batter runs plus the 1 No-ball extra (digest 8AD4729A). Counterfactual: with no bat or person contact, the 4 batter runs remain (boundary allowance subsumes the 2 completed runs), but the No-ball extra is not scored; the delivery becomes legal and counts in the over, the bowler is debited only the 4 batter runs, and all other facts are unchanged.

r25q_abfdb8ef05850f72da.explanation: CASE-E354EFAE6C (18:00, over 34): no No-ball or Wide call, so the delivery is legal and counts in the over. The ball touched the striker's bat, two runs were completed, then a fielder's throw at the wicket went for a boundary with the agreed allowance of 4; the batters had crossed at the instant of the throw. Under Law 19.8 (digest A7F3AEEE) the boundary allowance subsumes all prior movement, so 4 batter runs are recorded (Law 19.6-19.7, digest A5859EFC) and the wicket stands as RUN_OUT with the ball live at the moment of the throw. Counterfactual: with the batters not crossed at the instant of the throw, the run in progress is not added; the boundary allowance of 4 still subsumes the 2 completed runs, so the total remains 4 batter runs, with all other facts and the RUN_OUT dismissal unchanged.
